transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes, there is most likely something you should clean first. The 'funny smell' combined with poor drying is a common sign of restricted airflow on a washer-dryer. When the air can't flow freely through the drum, fluff builds up and gets scorched by the hot drying element, creating that odour, while the dampness stays trapped in the clothes. Please unplug the machine for safety. 1. Clean the lint filter (usually behind a small door at the bottom front corner). Remove all fluff.
2. If your model has a condenser unit (often located just above or next to the lint filter), remove it and rinse it under warm water until the water runs clear. Let it dry completely before putting it back. Once you've done this, try drying a smaller load (about half of what you usually wash). If the smell goes away and the clothes come out dry, it was just a blockage.

I didn't know the filter needed cleaning, so I've never done it. The smell is more like burning dust or scorched fabric, and the top of the machine gets very hot. I think I saw a faint haze near the door seal once too, but I've kept using it. Is that a problem?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes, that is a problem. A burning smell and the top of the machine getting very hot are signs of overheating, likely caused by fluff blocking the airflow path so it scorches on the heating element or internal components. Because there is an active burning smell and excessive heat, I must advise you to stop using the machine immediately for drying cycles until a qualified engineer has checked it. Continuing to run it risks damaging the appliance further or creating a fire hazard. 1. Clean the lint filter thoroughly as described before.
2. If your model has a condenser unit (usually above or next to the lint filter), remove it and rinse it under warm water until clear. Let it dry completely before replacing it.
3. Check the pump filter at the bottom front corner (have towels ready for any water) and clean out any fluff or debris.

candidates: Lint filter/condenser blocked causing restricted airflow and scorching fluff smell (high)
Overloaded drum or poor spin leaving clothes too wet to dry effectively (medium)
